histoire: Our mother supports our card business and talks about it a little too much at City Hall.
Our father doubts the value of cardboard but spends a fortune on his barbecue.
Our grandfather has kept every cable since 1987. A retired mechanic, he enjoys sharing his tricks.
Our grandmother diplomatically clears out the attic. She remembers every promise Frank ever made.
A firefighter who stays calm during emergencies, less so when assembling furniture. Jennifer's husband.
The grocery store manager. She knows her customers' habits and sometimes forgets to take a break.
Our childhood friend dreams of exploring other towns. She sometimes works at the cafe.
Ashley's little brother treats card trading like a stock exchange. Noah checks his calculations.
Dylan and Lily's mother prefers a straightforward sale to twenty messages. Debbie and Bob help her a lot.
He sells his played cards to fund a computer. Lily occasionally reveals their trip through the washing machine.
Dylan's little sister invents families for her figurines and tells the truth at exactly the wrong moment.
A retired mail carrier, meticulous collector and Matt's father. He values honesty over big speeches.
A former librarian and Gary's wife. She knows exactly how much his collection costs.
Gary's son and Megan's husband. He buys nostalgic collectibles for Chloe's college fund; she would prefer a bicycle.
A nurse, Jake's sister and Chloe's mother. She appreciates punctual people and short messages.
Matt and Megan's daughter loves animals, her grandparents and the bicycle she does not have yet.
Megan's brother shares a house with Ryan and Brittany. He launches a new business every week but remains a reliable friend.
Jake's roommate restores a car that consumes his savings and corrects his friend's business ideas.
A sarcastic, loyal waitress saving for training. She keeps track of the household grocery bills.
A car salesman and Karen's husband. He retells every negotiation he won and mysteriously forgets the others.
A real estate agent and Chad's mother. She prepares a file for everything, including defending the neighbors.
He works at the cafe and wants to leave the family home. He admires Ryan's independence.
The card shop owner gladly gives advice, but she will not bankroll bad decisions.
Linh's husband works remotely as an accountant. He considers cards irrational and spends too much on his garden.
Linh's daughter and Ashley's friend would rather draw monsters than track their prices.
Linh and Daniel's son records his trades with Tyler, but his favorite card can make him forget caution.
A retired seamstress and Isabel's mother. She knows how every neighborhood story began, rarely how it ended.
A retired mason, Rosa's husband and Frank's friend. His hearing improves when the offer goes up.
The Garcias' daughter works at City Hall. She turns Debbie's grand plans into achievable tasks.
Isabel's husband sells hardware. Every two months he changes hobbies and sells the previous equipment.
Isabel and Dave's daughter studies communications. She photographs his items but refuses to write all his listings.
A former bus driver and Denise's mother. She still recognizes adults by their childhood mischief.
Gloria's daughter and Marcus's wife is patient in class, but would like to shop without discussing school.
The cafe cook and Denise's husband is generous, but takes criticism of his barbecue sauce personally.
Denise and Marcus's son, Dylan's friend, is looking for equipment to make music.
Jayden's little sister loves insects and secrets she cannot keep.
Ben's husband is a self-employed gardener. He defends natural spaces against Carol's very specific requests.
Ethan's husband, Alice's father and Linh's employee loves card history so much that he forgets to sell them.
Ethan and Ben's daughter invents board-game rules and compares her parents' spending.
Dale's brother repairs almost anything and considers the landfill a personal defeat.
Earl's brother works at the recycling center. With permission, he salvages more objects than they can repair.
Scott's wife runs a home hair salon. She hears many secrets and hates being called a gossip.
The local police officer and Nancy's husband talks through disputes, except those involving school sports.
Nancy and Scott's daughter, Ashley's friend, wants to work and become independent. She stays frank with us.
Hailey's little brother always quotes the highest sale price and hides the card he overpaid for.
Amanda's mother organizes the flea market. She replaced chaos with rules almost as long as the street.
Debbie's husband, a retired road worker, loves his grandchildren and hates moving the same barrier three times.
A newcomer working remotely. He came for peace and quiet and is already fixing the neighbors' devices.
Kevin's wife wants to fit in, accepts too many invitations and sometimes mixes up their times.
Kevin and Rachel's son is new at school. He knows dinosaurs and discovers cards with Tyler and Noah.
A retired bank employee and Amber's grandmother. She seems distracted until it is time to count the money.
An illustrator staying with Dorothy. She is stabilizing her income and discovering her grandmother negotiates better.
A maintenance worker, Trevor's father and Mike's friend. He fixes the consequences of other people's good ideas.
A reseller who moved back in with his father after a setback. An opportunistic rival who knows how quickly reputations disappear.
Doug's wife works in administration from home. She loves rules and wages a very polite war against Daniel's garden.
A skilled but distracted technician and Carol's husband. He lends tools, then searches every neighbor's house for them.
Linda's friend is clearing her house before moving. Her stand overflows with linens and memories.
Marlene's husband helps her sell while buying tools from neighboring stands.
Denise's friend sells her children's clothes and toys. She knows exactly which pieces every game is missing.
Tasha's husband works in a warehouse. He packs his old games perfectly and forgets their prices.
Dorothy's former neighbor gives every object an embellished story, but describes its condition honestly.
June's grandson, a librarian, carries her boxes and makes sure she can rest.
Ryan's acquaintance loves music, sells modest instruments and spots fake expertise.
Luis's wife loves sewing. Her half of the stand is perfectly organized, unlike the other half.
Amber's friend is clearing her room before studying elsewhere. She still hesitates to sell some books and figurines.
Mike's former colleague is clearing a family garage. He sounds gruffer than he really is.
Gloria's friend is emptying a room. She always asks her children before selling their keepsakes.
Ben's board-game-loving friend provides far too much explanation for one-dollar items.
Marcus's former colleague and a father wants to drive home with a car empty of toys and sports gear.
Karen's friend has downsized. She appreciates considerate buyers without accepting every offer.
Linh's customer specializes in older editions. He speaks little and respects honest descriptions.
Unrelated to Amanda. She collects specific illustrations and remembers sellers who pay attention to her taste.
Trevor's rival inspects quickly and negotiates hard. Rushing sometimes makes him miss a detail.
Emma's friend is a student on a tight budget. She prefers trades and careful inspections.
Gary's former colleague has collected the same monster forever. His binder is very repetitive.
Ruby's mother learns about editions alongside her daughter and refuses to let anyone exploit her inexperience.
Olivia's daughter is always accompanied. She chooses cute monsters without checking their prices.
Jayden's friend attends high school in another town. He saves for one particular card and sells duplicates.
Nicknamed Spreadsheet, he loves average prices but sometimes forgets language or condition. Ben corrects him.
She buys damaged cards for their illustrations. Cleaning does not make her forget the damage.
Gloria's friend is building an album for his grandson and appreciates explanations without condescension.
Linh's wealthy but demanding customer buys rarely and knows exactly what she wants.
The cafe owner lives elsewhere. He lets Marcus cook but returns with questionable menu ideas.
Chris's colleague loves board games and sometimes visits the flea market after his shift.
Scott's colleague knows the local disputes and punctures dramatic speeches with dry humor.
The mail carrier knows addresses better than names. He notices our packages but never shares the neighbors' mail.
A bus driver and Gloria's former colleague. She knows the children's habits and will not wait forever.
The grocery delivery driver jokes with Jennifer but needs his access kept clear. He collects miniature trucks.
Doug's colleague now labels every tool after spending a week working with him.
A home-care nurse and Megan's former colleague. Her visits stay private; she never spreads confidences.
Ron's backup criticizes the old landscaping before asking where to get coffee.
A regional administrator and colleague of Susan and Isabel. She wants short answers in a talkative village.
Mike's sister, our aunt. She defends our project, then quietly asks whether we have done the math.
Mike's cousin walks with Doug and describes trips he has postponed for years.
Bob's sister sometimes helps at the flea market. She can contradict Debbie without triggering a meeting.
The Garcias' grandson and Madison's cousin. An apprentice cook who exchanges recipes with Marcus.
Amber's friend studies architecture. She comes to sketch the village and notices absurd design decisions.
Nina's brother is a weekend photographer. He often ends up discussing the water tower with Antonio.
Ethan's birdwatching acquaintance. One lawn mower is enough to make him move to another part of the park.
Dorothy and Gloria's friend is a retired music teacher. She recognizes misidentified instruments at the flea market.
